questions.explain: The ORDER BY expression must exactly match the indexed VECTOR_DISTANCE call, the metric must match the index metric, and TOP(@k) must be present — verify with the actual plan looking for the vector index seek operator.
options: ORDER BY matches the indexed expression, metric matches the index metric, TOP(@k) present — verify via the actual execution plan
Any ORDER BY works with a vector index
TOP is optional
Metric mismatches are harmless
questions.q: What are the requirements for the optimizer to use the vector index?

questions.explain: Rule of thumb: filter selecting more than ~5% of the corpus → pre-filter; less than ~5% → post-filter with oversampling; ultra-selective (hundreds of rows) → skip the index and brute-force.
options: Always pre-filter
Always post-filter
Pre-filter above ~5% selectivity, post-filter with oversampling below it, brute-force for ultra-selective filters
Filtering is not supported with vector search
questions.q: When should you pre-filter vs. post-filter vs. brute-force metadata constraints?

questions.explain: Stage 1: ANN oversample top 50–100; stage 2: RRF fusion with the full-text arm; stage 3: cross-encoder rerank of top 20–30 (50–200 ms) gated on query complexity, logging the rerank delta.
options: Rerank every query with the biggest model
ANN oversample → RRF fusion → optional cross-encoder rerank gated on complexity, logging the rerank delta
Skip ANN and rerank the whole corpus
Reranking never helps

questions.explain: Sample 200 queries; compute brute-force top-10 vs. index top-10; recall = overlap/10 as a scheduled job; set per-workload search lists and operate at the knee of the recall-vs-latency curve.
options: Guess a search list size once
Maximize latency regardless of recall
Use the same search list for all workloads
Benchmark recall vs. brute force on 200 queries, set per-workload search lists, operate at the curve's knee
questions.q: How is the DiskANN recall/latency tradeoff tuned?

questions.explain: Work bottom-up: is the content in the corpus → is it embedded → brute-force rank check (missed at rank ≤10 means widen search list; rank 347 means chunking/embedding problem) → query quality → execution plan and statistics.
options: Corpus → embedded → brute-force rank → query quality → execution plan; UPDATE STATISTICS after bulk loads
Rebuild the index first, always
Blame the embedding model first
Increase TOP until it works
